name: DataList
summary: The one way to show rows of records: Cynco UI's tray table on wide containers, one stacked card per row on narrow ones.
use: Any list of documents, accounts, transactions or lines you can describe as columns and rows. Don't hand-build <table> markup in a screen; declare columns and let DataList handle layout, selection, totals and the narrow-width card view. When the rows come from a TanStack table instance, use `DataTable`; for a handful of static rows, use the `Table` primitives.
provide: columns (key, header, cell, align, className, mobile: title | value | badge | meta | hidden | table | stacked, stackedAs, stackedCell, stackedLabel), rows, getKey; optional stackBelow (sm…3xl or never, default xl = 36rem of container width), column nowrap (keep IDs and dates on one line in the table), onRowClick (the primary cell, or the title when stacked, becomes the row's button; a click anywhere else on the row opens it too), column primary (the row header and button cell; default the first table column), column sortDirection (ascending | descending | none, announced as aria-sort on the header; DataList doesn't sort), isRowSelected, rowClassName, leading / leadingHeader (checkbox), trailing (row menu), totals ({label, [columnKey]: node} — a column-aligned tfoot in the table, a bold summary card when stacked), footer, empty, caption, dense / density (compact | default | comfortable; defaults from DensityProvider), stickyHeader + maxHeight (rows scroll, headers and totals stay put), className and any div props.
notes: Responds to its own container (CSS container queries), so the same list works in a page, a side sheet and on a phone. The primary column renders as the row header (th scope=row). Rows are never focus stops themselves: with onRowClick the primary cell holds a real button (focus-ring-inset), so screen readers announce it and the row's checkbox and menu aren't nested inside a focusable row. Selection without a leading checkbox is aria-current on that button. Leading/trailing cells and any control inside a row keep their clicks; keep a clickable row's primary cell free of links and buttons.

keys.does: Reaches the row's primary cell, which becomes a real button when onRowClick is set, and the scrolling region itself when the rows overflow it.

a11y.screenReader: The primary column renders as the row header (th scope="row"), column headers are th scope="col" and carry aria-sort from each column's sortDirection, and a trailing actions column gets an sr-only "Actions" header. A clickable row is never itself the focus stop, so its primary cell holds the button and the row's checkbox and menu are not nested inside a focusable row. Selection without a leading checkbox is reported as aria-current, and caption becomes an sr-only table caption and the label for the stacked list and for the scrollable region.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: Container width below which rows stack. Default `xl` (36rem). `never` keeps the table (it scrolls sideways).

props.name: onRowClick
props.description: Opens a row. The primary cell (table) or title (stacked) becomes a real button, so the row is reachable with Tab and announced as actionable; a click anywhere else on the row does the same.

props.name: rowClassName
props.description: Extra classes per row, in both layouts (e.g. dim inactive rows).

props.name: leading
props.description: Leading cell per row (e.g. a checkbox) — shown in both layouts.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Trailing cell per row (e.g. a row menu) — shown in both layouts.

props.name: totals
props.description: A totals row, keyed by column key. Renders column-aligned in the table (`tfoot`) and as a bold summary card in the stacked layout. Use `label` for the first cell's text.

props.name: footer
props.description: Free footer under the table / list, inside the tray.

props.name: dense
props.description: Compact rows. Defaults from the nearest DensityProvider.

props.name: density
props.description: Row density (overrides `dense` and DensityProvider).

props.name: stickyHeader
props.description: Keep the column headers (and totals) in view while the rows scroll. Needs `maxHeight`.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Scroll the rows inside this height (any CSS length, e.g. "24rem"); headers and totals stay put when `stickyHeader`.

name: StatTile
summary: One KPI (label, value, optional unit, sub line, badge and status dot) and StatGrid, the auto-fitting grid that holds them.
use: Rows of headline figures above a list or report. Put tiles in a StatGrid so they go 4-up on a page, 2-up in a sheet and 1-up on a phone.
provide: StatTile: label, value, optional unit, sub, badge, tone (green | blue | red | orange | amber | yellow | purple | pink | fuchsia | neutral), dot (any CSS colour; prefer tone), negative, className, div props, children (e.g. a sparkline). StatGrid: min (sm 9rem | md 11rem | lg 14rem tile width), mode (fit — default, tiles stretch to fill the row; fill — keep empty tracks to align with other grids), className, div props.
notes: The value wraps only between words (after "RM"), never mid-number, and never truncates; it steps up a size once the tile is 13rem wide.

props.name: unit
props.description: Small suffix after the value, e.g. "MYR" or "days".

props.name: sub
props.description: Small line under the value.

props.name: badge
props.description: Chip or delta at the top right.

props.name: tone
props.description: Leading status dot, by status tone.

props.name: dot
props.description: Leading status dot as any CSS colour or var() (prefer `tone`).

props.name: negative
props.description: Paint the value as negative/error text.

name: SectionPanel
summary: A titled card whose header actions wrap under the title when the container is narrow.
use: Grouping a chart, a detail list or a small table under a heading with actions. Use flush for content that runs edge to edge (tables).
provide: title, description, actions, flush, className, children and any section props.
notes: Named SectionPanel so it never collides with the AI kit's flow-canvas Panel.

props.name: actions
props.description: Rendered at the right of the header; wraps under the title on narrow containers.

props.name: flush
props.description: Remove body padding (for tables and lists that run edge to edge).

name: KeyValueList
summary: A label/value list: side by side when there's room, label above value below 16rem.
use: Totals blocks, document detail rails, payment summaries.
provide: items ({label, value, negative, strong}), className.
notes: Values are tabular-nums and right-aligned; negative uses text-error-text, strong makes a total row.

props.name: items
props.type: Array<{ label: ReactNode; value: ReactNode; negative?: boolean; strong?: boolean }>

name: ActionBar
summary: ActionBar is a row of controls that wraps instead of overflowing; ScrollRow is a single row that scrolls sideways (tabs, steppers, chips).
use: ActionBar for page and card toolbars. ScrollRow when the items must stay on one line in order, like status tabs or a stepper.
provide: className, children and any div props (both).
notes: ScrollRow hides its scrollbar; give it a role (tablist, list) and labels when it carries navigation.

name: ToneDot
summary: A 6px dot (or square) in one of Cynco UI's status tones; toneBg exposes the same background classes for bars and legend keys.
use: A small colour cue next to text that already says the state (account type, autosave, aging bucket).
provide: tone, square, className and any span props (title for a hover hint).
notes: Decorative (aria-hidden): the meaning must also be in nearby text.

props.name: square
props.description: Square corners (StatusChip style) instead of a round dot.

name: Button
summary: Cynco's one button: six variants on Base UI's Button, 28px tall by default.
use: Use `primary` for the single main action of a view or sheet, `secondary` for everything else, `muted` and `skeleton` for quiet toolbar actions, `destructive` only for irreversible deletes, `dotted` for "add another" slots.
provide: Children (label, optional Phosphor icon at 14px). Optional `isLoading` (shows `SmallSpinner`, keeps width), `disabled`, `size` (`md` 28px · `sm`/`icon` 24px), `render`/`asChild` to render as a link.
notes: Primary = `primary` fill with `primary-foreground` text, a 135° sheen and `shadow-sm`; secondary = `interactive-secondary` with `input` border and `btn-secondary-shadow`. Radius `rounded-lg` (= `radius`). One primary per surface.

keys.does: Activates the button.
Reaches the button even while it is loading, because a loading button is kept focusable instead of natively disabled.

a11y.screenReader: Nothing in the component supplies an accessible name, so the label is whatever you put inside it and an icon-only button needs an aria-label of your own. While isLoading, the button carries aria-busy, is disabled, and stays focusable with aria-disabled rather than the native disabled attribute. The label is only faded to transparent behind the spinner, so it still reads as the button's name.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Radix compatibility: render the single child element instead of a `<button>`.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Swaps the label for a spinner and disables the button, while the label stays its accessible name.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render instead of a `<button>` (Base UI).

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Keep the button in the tab order while disabled (Base UI). Set automatically while `isLoading`.

name: ButtonGroup
summary: Joins adjacent buttons, inputs or selects into one segmented control.
use: Segmented choices that act as one unit (date ranges, split buttons).
provide: Buttons/inputs as children; `orientation` horizontal (default) or vertical. `ButtonGroupText` and `ButtonGroupSeparator` for labels and dividers.
notes: Inner radii and duplicate borders are removed automatically.

name: IconButton
summary: A Button with a leading or trailing icon slot, sized for Cynco's 14px Phosphor icons, and an optional tooltip.
use: Any action whose icon helps scanning: "New invoice", "Filter". Icon-only for compact toolbars, with `tooltip` so it still has a name.
provide: All Button props plus `icon`, `rightIcon`, `iconOrientation` (`left` · `center` · `right`), `tooltip` and `tooltipSide`.
notes: An icon-only button with a string `tooltip` takes that text as its `aria-label` unless you pass one. Use `skeleton` for icon-only actions inside rows.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: A hint on hover and focus. On an icon-only button it also names the button when no `aria-label` is given.

props.name: tooltipSide
props.description: Which side the tooltip opens on.

props.description: Radix compatibility: render the single child element instead of a `<button>`.

props.description: The element to render instead of a `<button>` (Base UI).

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Keep the button in the tab order while disabled (Base UI). Set automatically while `isLoading`.

name: ShortcutButton
summary: A primary or secondary Button that shows and binds a keyboard shortcut.
use: Sheet and dialog submit actions (`metaShortcut="enter"` → ⌘/Ctrl ↵) and page-level "new" actions (`singleShortcut="n"`).
provide: `children`, `metaShortcut` or `singleShortcut`, `variant` (`primary` · `secondary`), `onClick`, `isLoading`.
notes: The shortcut is registered while mounted; the keycap renders inside the button. A bare-letter `singleShortcut` never fires while typing in a field and follows the user's single-key shortcuts switch (WCAG 2.1.4, `useCharacterKeyShortcuts`, set in ShortcutsDialog): when it is off the key stops firing and the keycap and aria-keyshortcuts are dropped. ⌘/Ctrl chords and named keys like Escape always work. The shortcut triggers a real click, so `onClick` and form submit behave exactly as a mouse click.

summary: A text-link-style action with an optional small icon.
use: "Add line", "Edit" links inside forms and sheets where a full button is too heavy.
provide: Button attributes plus `icon`; children is the label.
notes: Text in `tertiary-foreground`, `primary` on hover.

name: PanelButton
summary: A large, tactile tile button with screws and seams; the selected tile takes a primary border and a check mark in its corner.
use: Picking one of a few big options in onboarding (business type, tax registration).
provide: `isSelected`, `onClick`, `icon` (Phosphor duotone, 20px), and an `aria-label` (the tile is icon-only).
notes: Selection is exposed as `aria-pressed` and shown by the corner check mark, not by colour alone. The mark sits slightly outside the tile, so leave a few pixels of room around it.

name: GroupedTabButton
summary: A segmented tab control: equal-width options in a single pill track.
use: Switching a small set of mutually exclusive modes (period, chart range).
provide: `value`, `onValueChange`, `options` [{value, label?, icon?, disabled?}].
notes: Fills its container width; constrain the parent.

props.name: options
props.type: Array<{ value: V; label?: ReactNode; icon?: ReactNode; ariaLabel?: string; disabled?: boolean }>

name: Input
summary: The single-line text input: 28px, `interactive-secondary` fill, `input` border.
use: Every text field. Use `variant="destructive"` for validation errors, `headless` inside composite fields.
provide: Native input props, `variant`.
notes: Built on the shared input surface (border, radius, placeholder colour and focus treatment are the same ones SelectTrigger and Textarea use). Focus darkens the border and adds a soft 3px ring, never a coloured outline.

name: InputGroup
summary: An input with addons — icons, text, buttons — inside one bordered field.
use: Search fields, inputs with units or prefixes, inline submit buttons.
provide: `InputGroupAddon` (`align` inline-start · inline-end · block-start · block-end) holding `InputGroupText` or `InputGroupButton`, plus `InputGroupInput` or `InputGroupTextarea`.
notes: Uses `input-state-focus-within`.

name: InputOTP
summary: One-time-code input built on input-otp: grouped slots with an optional separator.
use: Sign-in OTP entry.
provide: `maxLength`, `value`, `onChange`; children `InputOTPGroup` of `InputOTPSlot index`, `InputOTPSeparator`.

a11y.screenReader: The slots are plain divs that paint the character and a blinking fake caret; the real control is the single input rendered by the input-otp package, so aria-label, autoComplete="one-time-code" and any error wiring belong on InputOTP itself. The separator carries role="separator", and the whole group dims when that input is disabled.

name: Textarea
summary: Multi-line text input with the input styling.
use: Descriptions and notes.
provide: Native textarea props.

name: LongInput
summary: A monospace-friendly textarea on `input-background` for JSON and long values.
use: Metadata editors and pasted config.
provide: Native textarea props.

name: TagInput
summary: A free-text input that turns entries into removable tags.
use: Lists of IDs or emails typed by the user.
provide: `value` string[], `onChange`, optional controlled `inputValue`.
notes: Enter or comma adds a tag; Backspace on empty removes the last.

keys.does: Commits what is typed as a tag.
On an empty field, removes the last tag.
Ends the word being typed and commits it as a tag.

a11y.screenReader: Tags change without focus moving, so every add and remove is announced through a role="status" region that stays mounted and only swaps its text, saying "{tag} added" or "{tag} removed". A paste of several words is announced as one list. Each tag's remove button is labelled "Remove {tag}", and because that button unmounts on use, focus is handed back to the text field.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled tags.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial tags for uncontrolled use.

name: TagSelect
summary: A multi-select shown as removable tags in a select-style field.
use: Choosing several known options (tags, branches, tax codes).
provide: `value`, `onChange`, `options` [{value,label}], `placeholder`, optional `formatTag`, `renderContent`, `className` (the field box) and any div props. Label it with `id` + a `Field`, or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`; `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid` also go on the trigger.
notes: The trigger fills the field from behind and announces "{n} selected"; the tags sit beside it, not inside it, so each "Remove {label}" button is its own tab stop. Removing a tag moves focus to the next tag, or back to the trigger.

keys.does: Reaches the field's trigger first, then each chip's remove button as its own stop.

a11y.screenReader: While chips are showing, the trigger holds an sr-only "{n} selected", so the field still reports its state even though the visible chips sit beside the combobox rather than inside it. Each remove button is labelled "Remove {label}" and is a 24 by 24 target, with its icon aria-hidden. Removing a chip moves focus to the neighbouring chip's button, or back to the trigger when no chip is left.

name: DateInputUnix
summary: A date (and optional time) picker whose value is a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.
use: Due dates, schedule dates, backdating.
provide: `unixDate` (ms or null), `setUnixDate`; optional `withTime`, `use24Hour`, `disablePastDates`, `minUnixDate`/`maxUnixDate`, `placeholder`.
notes: Opens a Calendar in a Popover.

a11y.screenReader: The trigger is a button that forwards id, aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby and aria-invalid, and reports open or closed through data-state. The popover is labelled "Choose date and time" or "Choose date" according to withTime. With time on, the period button names itself with the current period and the one it would switch to, for example "AM, switch to PM".

props.name: use24Hour
props.description: Show 24-hour clock (00–23) instead of 12-hour with AM/PM.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Override the empty-state label (e.g. "Now" when null means immediate).

name: TimePickerInput
summary: A two-digit time segment input (hours, minutes, 12-hour) with arrow-key stepping.
use: Composing a time picker; used inside DateInputUnix.
provide: `picker`, `date`, `setDate`, optional `period`, focus hand-off callbacks.
notes: Adapted from openstatusHQ/time-picker (MIT).

keys.does: Step the segment up or down by one.
Move focus to the previous or next segment.
Type the segment two digits at a time, then move focus on to the next one.
Leaves the segment, as do modifier chords such as paste and select all.

a11y.screenReader: Each segment is an input named for its own kind, so it is announced as "Hours", "Minutes" or "Seconds", and it falls back to a generated id and the picker name when the caller gives neither. The caret is hidden and every key other than Tab and modifier chords is handled by the component, so the value only changes through the arrow and digit keys. The file adds no live region, so announcing the assembled time is the surrounding control's job.

name: Calendar
summary: Month calendar on react-day-picker 8, selected day filled with `primary`.
use: Inside date popovers; inline when a date is the main input.
provide: react-day-picker props: `mode`, `selected`, `onSelect`, `defaultMonth`, `disabled`.
notes: Outside days shown by default.

a11y.screenReader: The dropdown caption renders an sr-only aria-live="polite" element holding the month name, which also labels the month grid, so paging announces the new month. The previous and next buttons take their names from react-day-picker's own labelPrevious and labelNext, and the month and year selects from labelMonthDropdown and labelYearDropdown, so a localised picker stays localised. Every chevron is aria-hidden and each day button keeps its own focus ring.

name: Select
summary: Base UI select with a 28px trigger and an `overlay` popup with check indicators.
use: Choosing one of a short, known list (payment terms, currencies). Use SearchableSelect past ~8 options.
provide: `value`/`defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `items` (labels for the value display); children `SelectTrigger` › `SelectValue`, `SelectContent` › `SelectItem`.
notes: Trigger uses `input-state-open`. `SelectItem indicator={false}` drops the checkmark.

keys.does: Moves focus to the trigger, which keeps its open treatment rather than its focus treatment while the popup is open, because focus has moved into the popup.

a11y.screenReader: The trigger shows the selected item's text, or the placeholder while the value is null, and takes its accessible name from you. A selected row draws a check icon unless you pass indicator false. The invalid treatment is keyed on aria-invalid so the state is announced as well as drawn.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The uncontrolled value of the select when it's initially rendered. To render a controlled select, use the `value` prop instead.

props.name: value
props.description: The value of the select. Use when controlled. `null` means nothing is selected (the placeholder shows) while staying controlled.

props.name: items
props.type: Record<string, string> | ReadonlyArray<{ label: string; value: string }>
props.description: Data structure of the items rendered in the select popup. When specified, `<Select.Value>` renders the label of the selected item instead of the raw value.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: `null` when the selection is cleared.

name: SearchableSelect
summary: A generic select with a search box, built on Popover + Command.
use: Choosing an account, item or customer from a long or remote list.
provide: `value`, `onValueChange`, `options`, `getOptionValue`, `getOptionLabel`; optional `renderOption`, `renderValue`, `onSearchChange` (server search), `header`/`footer`, `trigger`.
notes: `emptyText={null}` hides the empty state.

a11y.screenReader: The default trigger is a plain button that forwards id, aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby and aria-invalid from props, and sets no aria-expanded of its own because PopoverTrigger supplies that and aria-haspopup="dialog". The popup is labelled with the placeholder, and the search box is named by passing searchPlaceholder as the Command label, since cmdk always renders that label element and leaves the input unnamed without it. Each row carries aria-current for the chosen value, because cmdk's aria-selected tracks only the highlighted row.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled selection; null for none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial selection for uncontrolled use.

props.name: getOptionSearchTerms
props.description: Extra strings to match on, alongside the option's label and value.

props.name: renderValue
props.description: Renders the trigger's value. Return nothing for no selection and the trigger shows `placeholder`.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: `null` renders no empty state at all — the search input stands alone.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Replaces the default value-and-chevron button, e.g. with an icon button.

props.name: shouldFilter
props.description: Whether to filter options locally as the user types. Defaults to off when `onSearchChange` is set, since the caller is usually searching server-side.

name: Checkbox
summary: Square checkbox in three sizes, `primary` when checked.
use: Boolean options in lists and tables; use Switch for settings that apply immediately.
provide: `checked`/`defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange`, `size` (`sm` · `md` · `lg`), `disabled`.

keys.does: Toggles the checkbox, unless it is disabled.
Leaves the checkbox untouched so the chord reaches a sheet-level or form-level submit shortcut.

a11y.screenReader: The control carries no label of its own, so pair it with a Label or pass aria-label. The invalid treatment is keyed on aria-invalid, which you set and the component never sets for you.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

name: AreaCheckbox
summary: A checkbox with a title and description, optionally revealing children when checked.
use: Opt-in settings that need explanation (rounding, auto-numbering).
provide: `title`, `checked` / `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange`; optional `description`, `disabled` + `disabledReason` (tooltip), `children` (revealed when checked), `className` and any div props.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Initial state for uncontrolled use.

props.name: disabledReason
props.description: Disables the choice and says why, on a tooltip and to screen readers.

name: ToggleButton
summary: A button that stays pressed, with a check mark in its corner while it is on.
use: Toggling views and options in toolbars: show a chart, group rows, reveal filters.
provide: IconButton props plus `pressed` / `defaultPressed`, `onPressedChange`, `icon` and `iconOrientation` (`left` with a label, `center` icon-only, which needs `tooltip` or `aria-label`).
notes: It reports `aria-pressed` rather than posing as a checkbox; for a real checkbox use `Checkbox`. The corner mark means the state never rests on colour, and it sits slightly outside the button, so a clipping parent hides part of it.

props.name: pressed
props.description: Controlled pressed state.

props.name: defaultPressed
props.description: Initial pressed state for uncontrolled use.

props.description: Swaps the label for a spinner and disables the button, while the label stays its accessible name.

props.description: Radix compatibility: render the single child element instead of a `<button>`.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render instead of a `<button>` (Base UI).

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Keep the button in the tab order while disabled (Base UI). Set automatically while `isLoading`.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: A hint on hover and focus. On an icon-only button it also names the button when no `aria-label` is given.

props.name: tooltipSide
props.description: Which side the tooltip opens on.

name: RadioGroup
summary: Base UI radio group; items are small circles filled with `primary`.
use: Choosing one of 2–5 visible options.
provide: `value`/`defaultValue`, `onValueChange`; `RadioGroupItem value` children, each wrapped in a label.
notes: For options with descriptions use AreaRadioGroupItem.

keys.does: Moves focus to a radio, which draws a 2px focus-visible outline.

a11y.screenReader: Neither the group nor its items carry a label, so you supply the group's name and each option's label. The checked state belongs to the Base UI radio and is drawn by a small filled indicator inside the control.

name: AreaRadioGroupItem
summary: A radio option with a label and description line.
use: Tax treatment and behaviour choices in sheets.
provide: Inside RadioGroup: `value`, `label`, optional `description`, `disabled` + `disabledReason`.

name: Switch
summary: On/off switch, 36×20 (or 28×16 inside `SwitchSizeProvider size="sm"`).
use: Settings that take effect immediately.
provide: `checked`/`defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange`, `disabled`.
notes: Thumb uses `switch-thumb-on` when on.

keys.does: Toggles the switch.
Stops the toggle so the chord reaches a sheet-level submit shortcut instead.

a11y.screenReader: Nothing in the component names the switch, so pair it with a Label or pass aria-label. The thumb holds no text and exists only to draw the state, which the Base UI switch owns and exposes through data-checked and data-unchecked.

name: Dialog
summary: Centered modal on `overlay-dialog` with `overlay-dialog-shadow`.
use: Confirmations and short, blocking decisions. Longer forms go in a Sheet.
provide: `open`/`onOpenChange`; `DialogContent` (`showCloseButton`), `DialogHeader` › `DialogTitle` + `DialogDescription`, `DialogFooter` with secondary then primary/destructive buttons.

a11y.screenReader: DialogTitle and DialogDescription are what name and describe the popup, and they work visually hidden, which is how the command palette names its own dialog. The built-in close button is icon-only and carries the sr-only text Close.

name: Sheet

use: Most create and edit forms in Cynco (new customer, new item).
provide: `open`/`onOpenChange`; `SheetContent side`, `SheetHeader` › `SheetTitle` + `SheetDescription`, body, `SheetFooter`.

a11y.screenReader: SheetTitle and SheetDescription name and describe the panel. The close button is icon-only and carries the sr-only text Close. The sheet is portalled into document.body, or into the container an app names with SheetPortalContainerProvider or the portalContainer prop, so its place in the reading order follows that container.

name: Popover
summary: A floating panel on `overlay` anchored to a trigger.
use: Inline details, small forms and pickers.

name: Tooltip
summary: Short label shown on hover/focus; delay 0 by default.
use: Naming icon-only controls and clarifying terms.
provide: `TooltipTrigger` (with `render`) and `TooltipContent` (`side`, `align`). `Tooltip` brings its own provider.
notes: Keep it to one line.

a11y.screenReader: The tooltip adds no aria of its own, so the trigger still needs its own accessible name. The provider's delay defaults to 0, and a Tooltip rendered outside a provider wraps itself in one.

name: HoverCard
summary: A richer hover preview (Base UI PreviewCard).
use: Previewing a customer or invoice from a link.
provide: `HoverCardTrigger`, `HoverCardContent` with `align`/`side`.

a11y.screenReader: The content renders as a Base UI preview card in a portal, and the component adds no role, aria or sr-only text of its own. The Radix-style openDelay and closeDelay props are accepted and ignored.

name: DropdownMenu
summary: Base UI menu: items with icons, shortcuts, checkbox/radio items, submenus and a destructive variant.
use: Row actions and overflow menus.
provide: `DropdownMenuTrigger` (with `render`), `DropdownMenuContent`, `DropdownMenuItem` (`variant`, `shortcut`, `isLoading`), `DropdownMenuGroup` › `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`, `DropdownMenuSub`.
notes: A `DropdownMenuLabel` must sit inside a `DropdownMenuGroup`. Destructive items go last, after a separator.

keys.does: Runs that item and closes the menu, unless focus is in an input, a textarea or a contenteditable element.
Falls through to the Base UI menu's own typeahead when no item shortcut matches the key.

a11y.screenReader: Focus returns to the trigger when the menu closes, which is why the Radix onCloseAutoFocus prop is accepted and ignored. Checkbox and radio items draw their state with a check icon from the Base UI indicator, and a DropdownMenuLabel only names its group when it sits inside a DropdownMenuGroup. An item that is loading or shimmering is disabled.

name: Command
summary: cmdk command palette: search input, grouped items, shortcuts, footer hints.

a11y.screenReader: CommandDialog renders a DialogTitle and DialogDescription sr-only inside the popup, defaulting to Command Palette and Search for a command to run, so the dialog is named for as long as it is open. The list takes that same title as its label. CommandInput points aria-activedescendant at the option the list highlights at every moment, the first render included, so Enter never runs a row that was not read out. notes: It renders no element of its own, so `className` and the rest go to the popup.

props.name: children

name: SheetBackdrop

a11y.screenReader: The list, triggers and panels are Base UI's tabs, so the active tab is exposed as selected and tied to its panel. The component itself only adds the active styling, keyed on data-active, and a focus ring on the panel.

provide: `type`, `defaultValue`, `withSeparator`; `SheetAccordionItem value title description`.

name: Collapsible

use: "Advanced settings" and similar disclosures.
provide: `open`/`defaultOpen`, `CollapsibleTrigger` (with `render`), `CollapsibleContent`.

a11y.screenReader: The component is a thin pass-through to the Base UI collapsible, with data-slot names on the root, trigger and panel and no aria, label or sr-only text of its own. The trigger's own content is therefore its accessible name.

name: Carousel

use: Document template and onboarding galleries.
provide: `Carousel opts orientation setApi` › `CarouselContent` › `CarouselItem`, `CarouselPrevious`, `CarouselNext`.
notes: Leave horizontal room for the arrow buttons.

name: Badge
summary: A small rounded label in three variants.
use: Counts and neutral labels. Use StatusChip for states.
provide: `variant` (`default` · `muted` · `secondary`), `size` (`default` · `sm`), children.

name: BetaBadge
summary: A tiny "BETA" tag.
use: Next to the title of a feature in beta.
provide: Optional `className`.

name: IconBadge
summary: A badge with a leading or trailing icon.
use: Metadata like currency, branch, external links.
provide: `icon`/`rightIcon`, `variant` (`default` · `muted`), `position`.

name: StatusChip
summary: A neutral chip whose only colour is a small status square with a glyph.
use: Invoice, payment and filing states in tables and headers.
provide: `tone` (green · blue · red · orange · amber · yellow · purple · pink · fuchsia · neutral), `glyph` (check, clock, alert, x, pause, play, calendar, coins, …), `dashed` for drafts, label as children. `StatusChipIcon` is the square alone; `StatusRing` is a progress ring (`fraction` 0–1).
notes: Never colour the label — the square carries the state, and every state has a glyph and a word, so it never relies on hue. Tone hexes are fixed in the component (e.g. green #30a46c, blue #3e8bd9, red #e5484d, amber #e5a21f), not tokens.

a11y.screenReader: The chip is a plain span whose text is its accessible name, and the status square is an aria-hidden SVG, so the state is never carried by colour or by the glyph alone. A string child is also set as the title attribute, which gives the full wording back when the label truncates. The chip has no role or live region of its own, so a status that changes in place needs one on whatever holds it.

summary: A small numbered square for step lists.
use: Onboarding steps.
provide: The step number as children.

name: SectionTag
summary: A muted uppercase-free tag that labels a section.
use: Section headings inside sheets and editors.
provide: Children.

use: Inside search bars and toolbars to show applied filters.

name: InfoRow

use: Detail panels (customer, invoice).
provide: `label`, `value`, optional `icon`, `mono` for IDs.

name: Card

use: Grouping related content on a page.
provide: `CardHeader` › `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardAction`; `CardContent`; `CardFooter`.
notes: Radius `rounded-xl`, 1px `border`, `shadow-sm`.

use: Page- or section-level messages that stay visible.
provide: `variant`; an optional leading 16px icon, `AlertTitle`, `AlertDescription`, `AlertAction`.
notes: Tinted at 4% fill and 15% border; text stays `foreground` at 80%. Tone hues come from Tailwind (sky, emerald, amber, red), not tokens.

name: Table
summary: Plain table primitives (table, header, row, head, cell, footer, caption).
use: A small static table you write by hand. For a list of records driven by data, use `DataList`; for a TanStack-powered list page with sorting, selection and pagination, use `DataTable`.
provide: Native table element props; `flexibleTableColumns` on `Table`.

name: DataTable

use: A list page whose rows come from a TanStack table: invoices, customers, items. For a list you declare as columns and rows, without a table instance, use `DataList`; for a handful of static rows, use the `Table` primitives.
provide: A TanStack `table` instance (`useReactTable` + `getCoreRowModel` from `@tanstack/react-table`) passed via `DataTable.Provider config={{table, numberOfColumns, isLoading}}`; compose `Toolbar` › `Heading` + `Actions`, then `Container` › `Content` › `Header` + `Body`, with `Pagination` on the tray or `Footer` inside the table. Optional `onRowClick`, `getRowHref` + `linkComponent`, `enableSelection`, `virtualization`.
notes: Exported as `DataTable` so it does not clash with the `Table` primitive. `Pagination` pages the table instance by default and a cursor-paged result when you pass `cursor`; `Footer` is the same bar inside the table's own `<tfoot>`. Surfaces use the `table-*` tokens. Set `mobileCards` to swap rows for cards once the table's own container is under 640px.

keys.does: Reaches the first cell of each row, which is a link when getRowHref is set and a button when the row is clickable.
Activate that row target, and run the double-click action when the row has no single-click one.

a11y.screenReader: Table.Content names the table through aria-label or aria-labelledby, marks it aria-busy while loading, and keeps a polite live region that reports "Loading…", the empty-state text, or the row count. A sortable header is a button inside a th that carries aria-sort, and the caret icons are aria-hidden. The select-all box is labelled "Select all rows" and each row's box is named after that row's first text value so the labels stay distinct, while skeleton rows are aria-hidden.

name: ChartContainer
summary: shadcn chart wrapper for Recharts: maps a config to `--color-<key>` variables and supplies tooltip and legend content.
use: Revenue, expense and cash charts.
provide: `config` {key: {label, color | theme}} and one Recharts chart as child (import it from `recharts`); `ChartTooltip` + `ChartTooltipContent`, `ChartLegend` + `ChartLegendContent`.
notes: Colour series with `chart-series-1…8` in order; grid lines `chart-grid-stroke`.

name: Progress
summary: A thin progress bar, `primary` on a muted track.
use: Progress against a target, setup progress, import progress.
provide: `value` 0–100; optional `ProgressLabel`, `ProgressValue` children.

name: Skeleton
summary: A pulsing `muted` placeholder block.
use: Loading states shaped like the content.
provide: Sizing classes.

name: SmallSpinner
summary: A small circular spinner.
use: Inline loading (buttons use it automatically when `isLoading`).
provide: `size` in px.

name: LoadingShimmerText
summary: A line of text with a moving shimmer and spinner.
use: Long-running background work ("Syncing bank feed…").
provide: `text`.
notes: Uses the `.shimmer` gradient from the stylesheet.

name: CopyablePre
summary: A code block with a copy button pinned to its corner.
use: Install commands and multi-line snippets. For a single value inline, use `CopyButton`.
provide: `text`, plus any div props.

name: Label
summary: The one form label: a native `<label>`, with an optional required marker.
use: Naming any control. Inside a `Field` use `FieldLabel`, which binds it to the control for you.
provide: Children, `htmlFor` (the control's `id`) or a wrapped control, `required`, and any `<label>` props.
notes: `required` draws an asterisk and reads "(required)" to screen readers. Disabled styling follows the control through `peer-disabled:`, so put the label next to the control it names.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the control as required: an asterisk for sighted readers, the word for everyone else.

name: Field
summary: A form field: label, description, control and error, with the ids wired between them.
use: Every labelled control. It replaces hand-wiring `htmlFor`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid` on each field.
provide: `Field` (optional `invalid`) around `FieldLabel` (optional `required`, `hint`), `FieldDescription`, `FieldControl` wrapping the control, and `FieldError` while `invalid`.
notes: `FieldControl` is what hands the control its `id`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`, so the wiring cannot be forgotten. The description and the `hint` tooltip render outside the `<label>`, so the control's accessible name stays the label text. `FieldError` pairs a warning glyph with the words, so the error never rests on colour.

a11y.screenReader: FieldLabel is a native label bound to the control by id, so clicking it focuses the control and the control is named by it. FieldDescription and, while the field is invalid, FieldError are pointed at by the control's aria-describedby, and the control carries aria-invalid. `required` adds an sr-only "(required)" beside the asterisk. The `hint` tooltip is a real button, so keyboard focus opens it and Escape closes it.

name: PageHeader
summary: Page title row: icon + title (+ accessory) on the left, actions on the right.
use: Top of every list page; matches DataTable.Toolbar.
provide: `icon` (16px Phosphor fill in `subtle`), `title`, optional `titleAccessory`, actions as children.

name: PageContainer
summary: The main content panel that sits on `outer-background`.
use: Wrapping each page's content.
provide: Children.

name: SandboxBanner
summary: The blue tab hanging from the top edge that marks sandbox mode.
use: Shown on every page while working in a sandbox or demo company.
provide: Optional `label`, `icon`, `color`; `SandboxBannerAction` children.
notes: Fill is `sandbox`; text white.

props.name: color
props.description: Background colour, e.g. to tell environments apart.

name: Separator
summary: A 1px horizontal or vertical rule in `border`.
use: Dividing groups in toolbars and panels.
provide: `orientation`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The orientation of the separator.

name: ScrollArea
summary: A scroll container with thin custom scrollbars.
use: Lists inside fixed-height panels and popovers.
provide: Children; sizing classes; `ScrollBar orientation` for horizontal.

name: ResizablePanelGroup
summary: Resizable split panes (react-resizable-panels 4).
use: Editor layouts with a sidebar and canvas.
provide: `orientation`, `ResizablePanel defaultSize`, `ResizableHandle withHandle`.

name: AmountInput
summary: The money field accountants type into: accepts plain figures, “1,234.50”, accounting brackets “(500)”, “1.2k” and formulas like “=1200*1.08” or “100+250.50-20”, and commits an exact decimal string.
use: Anywhere a user enters an amount. While focused it shows exactly what was typed (with a live “= RM 1,296.00” hint for formulas); on blur or Enter it evaluates and shows the formatted, right-aligned figure.
provide: value / defaultValue (decimal string, "" for empty), onValueChange(value: string), currency? (adds the symbol prefix via InputGroup and formats the hint), allowNegative?, invalid? + errorMessage?, placeholder?, messages? ("below" for forms, "overlay" for grids), onAutoFill? (what “=” then Enter fills), onParseError?, inputClassName?, className (root) and any native input props (aria-*, name, disabled, onBlur…). Forwards its ref to the <input>.
notes: Maths via parseAmount / toSen (BigInt, half-up), so 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30. Fills its container's width; negatives display bracketed in text-error-text.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value: a decimal string ("1296.00") or "" for empty.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Uncontrolled initial value.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the evaluated decimal string when the figure is committed (blur or Enter) and changed.

props.name: currency
props.description: ISO code (e.g. "MYR"): shows the symbol as a prefix and in the live result hint.

props.name: allowNegative
props.description: Accept negatives ("-500", "(500)"). Default false.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Force the error styling (e.g. server-side validation).

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Message shown with `invalid`.

props.name: messages
props.description: Where the hint/error appear: in flow under the field (forms) or floating over the next row (grids).

props.name: onAutoFill
props.description: Typing `=` alone then Enter calls this; return a decimal string to commit it (e.g. the figure that balances a journal), or nothing if you've handled it yourself.

props.name: onParseError
props.description: Called when a commit is refused because the text isn't a valid amount.

props.name: inputClassName
props.description: Classes for the <input> itself (`className` goes on the root).

name: JournalGrid
summary: A keyboard-first journal line editor: searchable Account, Description, Debit and Credit cells with spreadsheet movement, auto-balance and a sticky footer showing Total Dr, Total Cr and whether the entry balances.
use: On the journal entry create/edit screen, and anywhere else lines must balance (opening balances, accrual templates, payroll postings).
provide: lines / defaultLines ({ id, accountId?, description?, debit?, credit? } with decimal-string amounts), onLinesChange(lines), accounts ({ id, code, name, type }), currency? (default MYR), minLines? (default 2), showShortcuts? (default true), className and native div props. Helper: journalTotals(lines) → { debit, credit, difference }.
notes: Keys: Tab / Shift+Tab move across cells and wrap to the next/previous line (and leave the grid past the ends); Enter moves down and adds a line on the last one; Shift+Enter up; ↑ ↓ change line in the same column unless the account list is open; mod+Enter adds a line below; mod+Backspace deletes the line (clears it at the minimum); Alt+B, or “=” then Enter in an amount cell, fills the figure that balances the entry; a Debit clears that line's Credit and vice versa, and a negative figure flips sides. Account cell: type a code or name, ↑ ↓ and Enter/Tab to pick, Alt+↓/F4 opens, Esc closes. Totals via sumAmounts; StatusChip shows Balanced / Out by RM x. Responsive: a grid on containers ≥ 36rem, a card per line below that (Debit and Credit side by side, each ≥ 6rem); the footer is sticky to the nearest scroll container.

keys.does: Moves to the next cell and wraps to the next line, and leaves the grid past the last cell.
Moves down the same column, and adds a line when already on the last one.
Move between lines in the same column.
Adds a line below the current one.
Deletes the line, or clears it when the entry is already at its minimum.
Fills the figure that balances the entry on the current line.

a11y.screenReader: Each line is a role="group" labelled "Line n" inside a group labelled "Journal lines", and every cell carries its own aria-label such as "Line 2 debit". An sr-only polite region reports what the keys did, for example "Line 3 added", "Line 2 deleted", "Negative figure moved to credit" or "Filled RM 1,200.00 credit to balance". The balance summary is itself aria-live="polite", so Balanced or Out by is announced without moving focus, and each line's delete button is out of the tab order with a label naming its line.

props.name: accounts
props.description: The chart of accounts for the Account picker.

props.name: lines
props.description: Controlled lines.

props.name: defaultLines
props.description: Uncontrolled initial lines (default: two blank lines).

props.name: minLines
props.description: Fewest lines kept; deleting below this clears the line instead. Default 2 (double entry).

props.name: showShortcuts
props.description: Show the keyboard legend under the footer. Default true.

name: InlineEditCell
summary: A table cell that edits in place: click, Enter or F2 to edit text or an amount, Enter or Tab to save, Esc to cancel, with a spinner while an async save is pending and a revert plus message when it fails.
use: Inside DataList / table cells for quick single-field corrections where opening a form would be slower: descriptions, references, amounts on draft documents.
provide: value, onSave(value) => void | Promise<void> (reject with an Error to revert and show its message), kind? ("text" | "amount"), currency? (amount read-out), placeholder?, allowNegative?, disabled?, aria-label (field name, e.g. "Description for EXP-2026-0311"), className and native div props.
notes: Keyboard: the cell is a button (visible focus ring, pencil on hover/focus); Enter, Space, F2 or click starts editing; Enter saves and returns focus to the cell; Tab or blur saves and moves on; Esc cancels. Amount mode uses AmountInput, so formulas work and an invalid figure stays in edit mode. Status (Saving… / Saved / error) is announced through aria-live; the saved tick fades after 1.6s. Fills its cell, so it follows DataList's table / stacked layouts.

props.name: value
props.description: The saved value (text, or a decimal string for `kind="amount"`).

props.name: onSave
props.description: Persist the new value. Return a promise to show a spinner; reject to revert and show its message.

props.name: currency
props.description: For amounts: formats the read-out ("RM 1,296.00").

props.name: allowNegative
props.description: For amounts: accept negatives. Default true.

name: CommandPalette
summary: A ⌘K / Ctrl+K command palette on Cynco UI's CommandDialog: jump to any area, create documents, reopen recent records and run app actions, with fuzzy search across labels, keywords, document numbers and amounts.
use: Mount once in the app shell and put a CommandPaletteTrigger in the header. Feed it recently opened records so accountants can type “inv 0142” or an amount like “3240” and land on the document. Use `inline` to embed the same search on a page (an empty state, a “Jump to” screen).
provide: CommandPalette: open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange; items (CommandPaletteItem[]: id, group — “Go to” | “Create” | “Recent” | “Actions” or your own heading, label, keywords, icon, shortcut such as "mod+k" or "g i", hint, href, disabled, onSelect); recent (CommandPaletteRecord[]: id, type — invoice | quotation | bill | credit_note | customer | vendor | journal | payment | item | account, number, label, status, amount as a decimal string, currency, keywords, href, onSelect); recentLimit (default 5); onSelect(item) to route with item.href / item.id; hotkey (default "mod+k", false to bind your own); placeholder; inline; className and native div props, spread on the inline root or on the dialog panel. CommandPaletteTrigger: label, shortcut, className and any button props (wire onClick).
notes: Keys: ⌘K / Ctrl+K toggles, ↑ ↓ move, Enter runs, Esc closes (clears the query when inline), a leading “>” narrows to actions. Search: every word must match a label, keyword, number or amount (prefix > word start > fuzzy subsequence; acronyms like “gl”, “pl”); groups re-rank by best match. Focus returns to whatever opened it. Rows drop status, amount, type and keycaps as the dialog narrows (container queries), so it stays one line from 320px up. Shortcut keycaps made of printable keys alone ("?", "g i") are hidden while the user has single-key shortcuts turned off; a printable-only `hotkey` is unbound then too.

keys.does: Toggles the palette, including while a text field has focus.
Move between results.
Runs the highlighted item.
Closes the dialog, or clears the query first when the palette is inline.
Typed at the start of the query, narrows the list to actions.

a11y.screenReader: The dialog carries an sr-only title and description naming the ">" prefix, and the search box is labelled "Search commands and records". cmdk does not announce its own empty state, so a stable polite region reports the result count as the query changes, saying "7 results" or "No results for" the query. A hotkey made only of printable keys is left unbound while the user has single-key shortcuts turned off, and the matching keycaps are hidden with it.

props.name: items
props.description: Commands: places to go, things to create, actions. Route in `onSelect` with `item.href` / `item.id`.

props.name: recent
props.description: Recently opened records, newest first. Searchable by number, name, status and amount.

props.name: recentLimit
props.description: How many recent records to list before the user types. Default 5.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called for every chosen item (after the item's own onSelect), e.g. to route to `item.href`.

props.name: hotkey
props.description: Shortcut that toggles the palette. Default "mod+k"; `false` to bind your own.

props.name: inline
props.description: Render in place (a card on the page) instead of as a ⌘K dialog.

provide: ShortcutsDialog: open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange; sections ([{title, items: [{keys, label}]}], keys like "mod+enter", "g i" for a sequence, or an array of alternatives); hotkey (default "?", false to bind your own); title; className. useGoToShortcuts(map, navigate, {enabled, timeout = 1200 ms, leader = "g"}): map keys are a letter after the leader or a full sequence ("c i"); returns {pending} so you can show “G…” while it waits. Items take an optional focusScoped: true for keys that only fire inside their own field (never shown as off). KeyboardShortcutsProvider (characterKeys / defaultCharacterKeys = true / onCharacterKeysChange) and useCharacterKeyShortcuts() → [enabled, setEnabled] control the single-key switch; isCharacterKeyShortcut(keys) tells you whether your own shortcut should honour it.

Sequences are ignored while typing, inside dialogs and menus, and with ⌘/Ctrl/Alt held; any other key or the timeout cancels. Sections flow into two columns once the dialog is 36rem wide. WCAG 2.1.4: the footer has a “Single-key shortcuts” switch. Off unbinds “?”, every useGoToShortcuts sequence and bare-letter ShortcutButtons, and marks those rows Off; ⌘/Ctrl chords and named keys are unaffected. With no provider the choice is saved in localStorage (cy-character-key-shortcuts) and syncs across tabs; pass characterKeys to store it yourself. When it is off, the dialog opens from the command palette or a button. Gate your own printable-only page shortcuts on useCharacterKeyShortcuts().

name: UndoToast
summary: "Do it, then offer Undo": a toast with the message, an Undo button (⌘/Ctrl+Z), an optional countdown and late commit — the real write runs in onCommit only if nobody undoes.
use: Mount UndoToastProvider once near the app root. On a destructive action, update the UI optimistically and call useUndoToast().show({message, onUndo, onCommit}); do the server call in onCommit. Keep real confirm dialogs only for actions that can't be held back (e.g. submitting to LHDN).
provide: UndoToastProvider: children, max (default 3; a 4th toast commits the oldest), duration (ms, default Infinity: stays until dismissed, undone or pushed out, per WCAG 2.2.1), viewport (default true; false to place <UndoToastViewport/> yourself), position (bottom-center | bottom-right | bottom-left). useUndoToast() → {show({message, onUndo, onCommit?, duration?, undoLabel?, id?}) → id, undo(id?), dismiss(id), count}. UndoToastViewport: position, className, section props. UndoToast (the presentational item): message, onUndo, onDismiss, onExpire, duration, undoLabel, showShortcut, paused, className, li props.
notes: Keyboard: ⌘/Ctrl+Z undoes the newest toast (left alone while typing in a field, where it is the field's own undo); F8 jumps to the newest Undo button; Esc on a focused toast dismisses (commits) it; focus returns to where it was. The countdown pauses on hover, on focus and while the tab is hidden; the stack is an aria-live="polite" list. Each toast settles exactly once; anything pending commits when the provider unmounts or on pagehide. No toast library — the countdown is a CSS animation whose end commits. Width is min(24rem, viewport − 2rem); hidden in print.

keys.does: Undoes the newest toast, unless the user is typing in a field outside the toast stack.
Moves focus to the newest toast's Undo button.
Dismisses the focused toast.

a11y.screenReader: The viewport is a section labelled "Notifications (F8)" wrapping an ol with aria-live="polite" and aria-relevant="additions text", so a new toast is read out without taking focus. The Undo button carries aria-keyshortcuts for the undo chord while its keycap is aria-hidden, the dismiss button is labelled "Dismiss", and the countdown bar is aria-hidden. When a toast closes while focus is inside it, focus moves to the next remaining Undo button, or back to the element named by returnFocusTo.

summary: Items KPI row: estimated margin on sales (or average profit margin), average revenue per item, highest earning item, most sold item, each over the trailing sales window.
use: Above the items list.
provide: `stats` {avgProfitMargin, avgRevenuePerItem, highestEarningItem, mostSoldItem}; optional `realizedMargins` {marginPercent, lineCount, belowCostItemCount}, `currency`, `windowDays`; optional `className` and native div props on the root.
notes: Responsive by container: StatGrid tiles auto-fit and never truncate.

props.name: stats
props.type: { avgProfitMargin: number | null; avgRevenuePerItem: Num; highestEarningItem: { name: string; revenue: Num } | null; mostSoldItem: { name: string; quantity: number } | null }

props.name: realizedMargins
props.type: { marginPercent: number | null; lineCount: number; belowCostItemCount: number }

name: InventoryFlowPanel
summary: Stock lifecycle in five steps (set up items, order and receive, record bill, dispatch goods, reconcile) with the GL reconciled / review state.
use: Top of the inventory workspace.
provide: `trackedItems` count and `isReconciled`; optional `className` and native section props on the root.
notes: Responsive by container: steps 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 per row by container width.

name: StockBalancesReport
summary: Stock balances by item and location (on hand, WAC to 4 dp, value, Healthy/Low/Negative) with the GL inventory vs stock ledger reconciliation strip.
use: Inventory workspace balances and reports.
provide: `balances` [{itemId, itemName, locationName, quantity, unitOfMeasure, weightedAvgCost, value, reorderPoint}], `reconciliation` {glBalance, subledgerBalance, difference, isReconciled}; optional `period`; optional `className` and native section props on the root.
notes: Balances table, per-item balance status and a reconciliation strip in one panel. Responsive: DataList for balances; the reconciliation strip wraps.

props.name: reconciliation
props.type: { glBalance: Num; subledgerBalance: Num; difference: Num; isReconciled: boolean }

name: PurchaseOrderStats
summary: Purchase order KPI row: total POs, drafts, approved total.
use: Top of the purchase orders list.
provide: `stats` [{status, count, total}]; optional `currency`; optional `className` and native div props on the root.
notes: Responsive by container: StatGrid tiles auto-fit.

props.name: stats
props.type: { status: string; count: number; total: Num }[]

name: PurchaseOrderLines
summary: Editable PO line items (description, qty, unit price, amount auto-calculated as qty × price) with remove, Add line item, and subtotal / SST / total.
use: Create or edit a purchase order; `readOnly` on the PO detail.
provide: `lineItems` [{id, description, quantity, unitPrice, amount}]; optional `defaultLineItems` and `onLineItemsChange` (uncontrolled when omitted), `readOnly`, `currency`, `taxAmount`; optional `className` and native div props on the root.
notes: The totals block mirrors the PO's subtotal/tax/total fields.

props.name: lineItems
props.description: Controlled lines.

props.name: defaultLineItems
props.description: Initial lines for uncontrolled use.

name: PurchaseOrderLinkedBills
summary: Bills linked to a purchase order: bill number, issue date, amount and bill status.
use: PO detail sidebar.
provide: `bills` [{id, billNumber, status, totalAmount, currency, issueDate}]; optional `currency`, `onRowClick(bill)`; optional `className` and native div props on the root.
notes: Responsive by container: built on DataList: a tray table from 36rem, a stacked card per bill below that.

name: PayslipSummary
summary: One payslip: gross, statutory deductions, net pay, employer cost; pay lines (earnings and EPF/SOCSO/EIS/PCB deductions); employee and employer contributions per scheme with Unverified flags; payment state and Mark paid.
use: Payslip drawer or detail on a payroll run.
provide: `payslip` {employeeName, reference, gross, statutoryDeductions, otherDeductions, net, employerCost, paymentStatus, paymentReference, lines, contributions} in integer sen; optional `month`, `canMarkPaid`, `onMarkPaid(reference)`; optional `className` and native section props on the root.
notes: Responsive by container: StatGrid tiles wrap; pay lines and contributions sit side by side from 42rem; the contributions are a DataList on the library's tray surface.

name: PayslipsRunTable
summary: A payroll run's payslips: employee and reference, gross, statutory, other deductions, net, employer cost and Paid/Unpaid, with run totals.
use: Payroll run page.
provide: `payslips` (PayslipSummary shape, sen); optional `payable` (false for correction runs), `onRowClick(payslip)`; optional `className` and native div props on the root.
notes: Responsive by container: DataList: table when wide, employee/net cards when narrow; totals wrap.

name: PayrollRemittancesPanel
summary: Owed to agencies: employee and employer shares a run remits per creditor (KWSP/EPF, PERKESO SOCSO and EIS, LHDN PCB, HRD Corp).
use: Payroll run page, after compute.
provide: `remittances` [{payable, label, employee, employer}] in sen; optional `className` and native section props on the root.
notes: Responsive by container: DataList stacks below 24rem; totals wrap.

props.name: remittances
props.type: { payable: string; label: string; employee: number; employer: number }[]

name: EInvoiceStatusCard
summary: LHDN MyInvois e-invoice state for an invoice or note per environment (valid, pending validation, rejected with LHDN errors, unconfirmed, cancelled, buyer-requested rejection), the validated UUID / long ID stamp, and Submit / Cancel (72-hour window) actions.
use: Invoice and credit/debit note detail sidebars (NoteEInvoiceCard).
provide: `credentialEnvironments` (sandbox|production), `byEnvironment` {status, documentUuid, longId, validatedAt, rejectionRequestedAt, rejectionReason, validationErrors, unconfirmed, withinCancelWindow}; optional `environment` / `defaultEnvironment` / `onEnvironmentChange`, `documentLabel`, `hasCorrection`, `onSubmit`, `onCancel`, `onCheck`; optional `className` and native div props on the root.
notes: Fetcher, retry hold and portal-settle flow are left to the caller. Validation stamp from templates/EInvoiceValidationBlock (QR omitted). Responsive by container: controls in a wrapping ActionBar; UUID and long ID break instead of overflowing.

props.name: credentialsHref
props.description: Where MyInvois credentials are set up; links the "not configured" message.

props.name: correctionHref
props.description: Where to raise the correcting credit note; links the "window has passed" message.

props.name: environment
props.description: Controlled environment whose filing the card shows.

props.name: defaultEnvironment
props.description: Environment shown on first render when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first credentialled one.

name: Artifact
summary: A titled container for something the assistant produced (a file, config or document), with actions and a close button.
use: Showing generated output beside or inside a chat.
provide: `ArtifactHeader` › `ArtifactTitle`, `ArtifactDescription`, `ArtifactActions` › `ArtifactAction` (`tooltip`, `label`, `icon` or children), `ArtifactClose`; `ArtifactContent`.

name: Canvas
summary: A React Flow canvas preset for agent workflows: dotted background, pan/zoom, delete keys.
use: Visualising multi-step agent or approval workflows.
provide: React Flow props: `nodes`, `edges`, `nodeTypes` (use Node), `edgeTypes` (use Edge), plus children such as Controls, Panel.
notes: Imports `@xyflow/react/dist/style.css`, so your bundler must handle CSS imports (Vite, Next.js and Astro do).

name: Node
summary: A Card-styled workflow node with optional connection handles.
use: Each step on a Canvas.
provide: `handles` {target, source}; `NodeHeader` › `NodeTitle`, `NodeDescription`, `NodeAction`; `NodeContent`; `NodeFooter`.
notes: Register it in `nodeTypes`; with handles it must render inside a Canvas.

name: Edge
summary: Two edge styles for the Canvas: `Edge.Animated` (a dot travels the path) and `Edge.Temporary` (dashed).
use: Connections between Nodes; Temporary for proposed links.
provide: Register as `edgeTypes={{animated: Edge.Animated, temporary: Edge.Temporary}}` and set each edge's `type`.
notes: Stroke uses `ring`.

name: Controls
summary: React Flow zoom/fit/lock controls styled for Cynco.
use: Inside a Canvas.
provide: React Flow Controls props.

name: Panel
summary: A floating panel pinned to a corner of the Canvas.
use: Canvas titles, run buttons, legends.
provide: `position` (`top-left` … `bottom-right`), children.

name: Toolbar
summary: A node toolbar that floats above a selected Node.
use: Edit/delete actions on a node.
provide: React Flow NodeToolbar props: `isVisible`, `position`; children buttons.

name: Connection
summary: The connection line drawn while dragging from a handle.
use: Pass as the Canvas `connectionLineComponent`.
provide: Nothing — React Flow supplies the coordinates.
notes: Only visible during a drag.

name: ChainOfThought
summary: A collapsible list of the assistant's reasoning steps with status, results and images.
use: Showing how an answer was reached.
provide: `open`/`defaultOpen`; `ChainOfThoughtHeader`, `ChainOfThoughtContent` › `ChainOfThoughtStep` (`label`, `description`, `status` complete · active · pending, `icon`), `ChainOfThoughtSearchResults` › `ChainOfThoughtSearchResult`, `ChainOfThoughtImage caption`.

name: Checkpoint
summary: A divider row marking a restorable point in a conversation.
use: Between messages, to roll back.
provide: `CheckpointIcon`, `CheckpointTrigger` (Button props + `tooltip`).

name: CodeBlock
summary: Syntax-highlighted code (Shiki, one-light / one-dark-pro) with line numbers and a copy button.
use: Code in assistant replies and tool output.
provide: `code`, `language`, `showLineNumbers`; `CodeBlockCopyButton` child.
notes: The bundle carries Shiki grammars for TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript, JSX, JSON, Bash, Python, CSS, HTML, Markdown, YAML, SQL and Go; other languages render as plain text.

name: CompactPromptInput
summary: A one-line prompt field with the submit button inline.
use: Small "ask about this" boxes without attachments.
provide: `value`, `onChange`, `onSubmit`, `placeholder`, `isLoading`.

name: Confirmation
summary: An approval request for a tool call, built on Alert.
use: When the agent needs a yes/no before acting (deleting, posting).
provide: `state` (AI SDK tool state), `approval`; `ConfirmationTitle` › `ConfirmationRequest` / `ConfirmationAccepted` / `ConfirmationRejected`; `ConfirmationActions` › `ConfirmationAction`.
notes: Each child renders only in its matching state.

name: Context
summary: A token-usage meter with a hover card breaking down input, output, reasoning and cache tokens and cost.
use: Showing how much of the model's context window is used.
provide: `usedTokens`, `maxTokens`, `usage`, `modelId`; `ContextTrigger`, `ContextContent` › `ContextContentHeader`, `ContextContentBody` (usage rows), `ContextContentFooter`.
notes: Cost uses tokenlens model prices.

name: Conversation
summary: A scroll container that sticks to the bottom as messages stream in.
use: The chat transcript.
provide: `ConversationContent` with Messages; `ConversationEmptyState` (`title`, `description`, `icon`); `ConversationScrollButton`.

name: Image
summary: Renders an AI SDK generated image from base64.
use: Images returned by an image model.
provide: `base64`, `mediaType`, `uint8Array`, `alt`, `className`.

name: InlineCitation
summary: Inline citation badges that open a card listing sources (with carousel for several) on hover, click or Enter, so keyboard users can reach every source.
use: Citing sources inside assistant text.
provide: `InlineCitationText`, `InlineCitationCard` › `InlineCitationCardTrigger sources`, `InlineCitationCardBody` › `InlineCitationSource` (`title`, `url`, `description`) or the carousel parts, `InlineCitationQuote`.

name: Loader
summary: A small spinning loader glyph.
use: While the assistant is working.
provide: `size`.

name: Message
summary: A chat message: user bubbles on the right, assistant replies as Markdown, with actions, branches and attachments.
use: Every chat turn.
provide: `from` (`user` · `assistant`); `MessageContent` › `MessageResponse` (Streamdown Markdown) ; `MessageActions` › `MessageAction` (`tooltip`, `label`); `MessageBranch*` for alternative replies; `MessageAttachments` › `MessageAttachment`.
notes: Mermaid diagrams inside Markdown are not bundled and render as nothing.

name: ModelSelector
summary: A command-palette dialog for choosing a model, with provider logos.
use: Model pickers in chat inputs.
provide: Dialog props; `ModelSelectorTrigger`, `ModelSelectorContent title` › `ModelSelectorInput`, `ModelSelectorList` › `ModelSelectorGroup heading` › `ModelSelectorItem` › `ModelSelectorLogo provider` + `ModelSelectorName`.
notes: Logos load from models.dev at runtime.

name: OpenIn
summary: A dropdown that opens the current query in ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, T3, Scira or v0.
use: "Open in…" next to docs or prompts.
provide: `query`; `OpenInTrigger`, `OpenInContent` › `OpenInChatGPT`, `OpenInClaude`, `OpenInCursor`, `OpenInT3`, `OpenInScira`, `OpenInv0`.

name: Plan
summary: A collapsible card describing a plan the agent proposes, with a shimmer while streaming.
use: Before running multi-step changes.
provide: `isStreaming`, `defaultOpen`; `PlanHeader` › `PlanTitle`, `PlanDescription` (strings), `PlanAction` › `PlanTrigger`; `PlanContent`; `PlanFooter`.

name: PromptInput
summary: The full chat composer: textarea, attachments, tools, model select, speech and submit with status.
use: The main chat input.
provide: `onSubmit(message)`, `accept`, `multiple`, `maxFiles`; `PromptInputBody` › `PromptInputTextarea`; `PromptInputFooter` › `PromptInputTools` (buttons, `PromptInputActionMenu`, `PromptInputSelect`, `PromptInputSpeechButton`) + `PromptInputSubmit status`; optional `PromptInputProvider` to control it from outside.

name: Queue
summary: A collapsible queue of pending and completed tasks or messages.
use: Showing what the agent will do next.
provide: `QueueSection` › `QueueSectionTrigger` › `QueueSectionLabel count label`, `QueueSectionContent` › `QueueList` › `QueueItem` › `QueueItemIndicator completed`, `QueueItemContent`, `QueueItemDescription`, `QueueItemActions`.

name: Reasoning
summary: The model's reasoning in a collapsible that auto-opens while streaming and reports how long it thought.
use: Reasoning models' thinking text.
provide: `isStreaming`, `duration`, `defaultOpen`; `ReasoningTrigger` (`getThinkingMessage`), `ReasoningContent` (string, Markdown).

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the collapsible panel is currently open. To render an uncontrolled collapsible, use the `defaultOpen` prop instead.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the collapsible panel is initially open. To render a controlled collapsible, use the `open` prop instead.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Event handler called when the panel is opened or closed.

name: Shimmer
summary: Text with a moving shimmer.
use: Short "working" labels while streaming.
provide: String children; `duration`, `spread`, `as`.

name: Sources
summary: A "Used N sources" disclosure listing source links.
use: Under answers that searched the web or docs.
provide: `SourcesTrigger count`, `SourcesContent` › `Source href title`.
notes: Collapsible: pass `defaultOpen` to show the list.

name: Suggestion
summary: A horizontal row of suggested prompts as pill buttons.
use: Empty chats and follow-up ideas.
provide: `Suggestions` › `Suggestion suggestion onClick`.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Swaps the label for a spinner and disables the button, while the label stays its accessible name.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Radix compatibility: render the single child element instead of a `<button>`.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render instead of a `<button>` (Base UI).

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Keep the button in the tab order while disabled (Base UI). Set automatically while `isLoading`.

name: Task
summary: A collapsible task with its sub-steps and file references.
use: Showing an agent's search or edit work.
provide: `TaskTrigger title`, `TaskContent` › `TaskItem` (with `TaskItemFile`).

name: Tool
summary: A collapsible card for a tool call: name, status badge, parameters and result as highlighted JSON.
use: Every tool call in a transcript.
provide: `ToolHeader` (`type`, `state`, `title`), `ToolContent` › `ToolInput input`, `ToolOutput output errorText`.
notes: States: input-streaming, input-available, approval-requested, output-available, output-error, output-denied.

name: WebPreview
summary: A mini browser: navigation buttons, URL bar, an iframe body and a collapsible console.
use: Previewing a page the agent built.
provide: `defaultUrl`, `onUrlChange`; `WebPreviewNavigation` › `WebPreviewNavigationButton tooltip`, `WebPreviewUrl`; `WebPreviewBody` (iframe); `WebPreviewConsole logs`.
notes: The demo leaves out the iframe body.
